front: Name the 6 Microsoft responsible AI principles (mnemonic FRIPTA).
back: Fairness, Reliability & safety, Inclusiveness, Privacy & security, Transparency, Accountability.

front: A speech-based agent also shows text captions so hearing-impaired users can use it. Which principle?
back: Inclusiveness - don't exclude any users.

front: A robot only acts when object-detection confidence exceeds a threshold. Which principle and why?
back: Reliability & safety - AI is probabilistic, so mitigate risk of harm with confidence thresholds.

front: Bank discloses that loans are assessed by AI and describes training-data features. Principle? How differs from accountability?
back: Transparency (users understand how it works + limits). Accountability = people/org answerable via a governance framework.

front: 4 harm categories in Foundry content filters + severity levels?
back: Hate & fairness, Sexual, Violence, Self-harm; severity safe/low/medium/high; applied to prompts AND completions.

front: What is a token and why isn't it the same as a word?
back: Unit of text with an integer ID: words, sub-words ('un'), punctuation, common sequences.

front: What does an embedding capture and how is similarity measured?
back: Semantic/linguistic meaning as a vector; similar meaning → similar direction; cosine similarity.

front: What does attention do in a transformer? What is multi-head attention?
back: Weights how much surrounding tokens influence each token (context); multi-head evaluates different vector elements in parallel.

front: How does an LLM produce a completion?
back: Repeatedly predicts the most probable next token given all previous tokens until an end token.

front: When choose an SLM over an LLM?
back: Focused/topic-specific tasks, local or on-device deployment, lower cost; LLMs generalize better but cost more.

front: System prompt vs user prompt?
back: System = set by app: role, tone, constraints, tools. User = end-user question/instruction answered within system rules.

front: How does a chat app keep multi-turn context if the model is stateless?
back: It resends conversation history (previous prompts+responses, often summarized) with each new prompt.

front: 3 components of an agent?
back: Model (brain/reasoning), Instructions (system prompt = job description), Tools (knowledge + action).

front: Which agent tool: current events / your PDFs / analyze a CSV and chart it / call your REST API?
back: Web search / File search (knowledge) / Code interpreter / OpenAPI tool or function calling (or MCP).

front: Learn's 4 prompt-engineering tips?
back: Be clear & specific; add context (topic, audience, format); use examples; ask for structure.

front: Stemming vs lemmatization?
back: Stemming chops suffixes mechanically (powering→power, may be non-word). Lemmatization returns valid dictionary form using linguistic rules (running→run).

front: TF-IDF formula and what a word in every document scores?
back: tf(t,d) × log(N/df(t)); appears in all docs → log(1)=0 → no discriminative weight.

front: Bigram example? Trigram example?
back: 'artificial intelligence'; 'natural language processing'.

front: Need consistent, deterministic structured text analysis in an automated pipeline: LLM or Azure Language?
back: Azure Language in Foundry Tools (purpose-built, statistical, deterministic). LLM for flexible multi-task/prototyping.

front: Which SDK method + property gives redacted PII text?
back: TextAnalyticsClient.recognize_pii_entities([...]) → result.redacted_text (+ entities with category, confidence_score).

front: What is MCP and what does the Azure Language MCP server need to connect?
back: Open standard linking agents (clients) to tools on servers; add 'Azure Language in Foundry Tools' tool and enter the Foundry resource name - no separate Language resource.

front: Extractive vs abstractive summarization?
back: Extractive picks original sentences (e.g., TextRank); abstractive writes new sentences (generative).

front: STT pipeline stages in order?
back: Audio capture → feature extraction (MFCC) → acoustic model (phonemes) → language model (words) → decoding (beam search) → post-processing.

front: TTS pipeline stages in order?
back: Text normalization → linguistic analysis (G2P phonemes) → prosody → waveform via neural vocoder.

front: Why does synthetic speech sound robotic?
back: Flat/monotone prosody (pitch, rhythm, stress) - not wrong phonemes.

front: Real-time vs batch transcription - when each?
back: Real-time for live audio/captions; batch for stored recordings (async, SAS URI, best-effort scheduling).

front: Speech SDK classes for STT vs TTS?
back: STT: SpeechConfig + AudioConfig + SpeechRecognizer (recognize_once). TTS: SpeechConfig(+voice name) + AudioOutputConfig + SpeechSynthesizer (speak_text_async().get()).

front: What is Voice Live?
back: Fully managed speech-to-speech API combining STT, a generative model you choose, and TTS in one real-time service (interruptions, avatars, actions).

front: How do you send a spoken prompt directly to a multimodal model?
back: Audio model (e.g., gpt-4o-mini-audio-preview): content part type input_audio with base64 data + format; modalities ['text','audio'].

front: Classification vs object detection vs semantic segmentation?
back: One label per image / labels + bounding boxes for multiple objects / label for every pixel (mask).

front: What does convolving a kernel do; what does the Laplace kernel do?
back: Weighted sum over each pixel patch → new image/feature map; Laplace highlights edges.

front: CNN layer order?
back: Conv filters → feature maps → pooling → flatten → fully connected → softmax probabilities; trained by loss over epochs.

front: How do diffusion models generate images?
back: Start from random noise, iteratively denoise guided by the prompt until image matches.

front: Responses API content types for an image question?
back: input_text + input_image (image_url = URL or base64 data URL); read response.output_text.

front: Video generation in Foundry: models + call pattern?
back: Sora / Sora 2; async job: POST /videos → poll GET /videos/{id} → download /content mp4.

front: OCR vs field extraction?
back: OCR finds/reads text (+ positions, confidence) without meaning; field extraction maps text to labeled fields (Vendor, Total) using position/semantics.

front: What is a Content Understanding analyzer and a schema?
back: Analyzer = reusable unit applying the same AI extraction logic; schema = fields (incl. nested) to extract, applied semantically.

front: Name analyzers for OCR text, invoice, audio, video.
back: prebuilt-read, prebuilt-invoice, prebuilt-audioSearch, prebuilt-videoSearch (also prebuilt-layout, prebuilt-receipt).

front: Why begin_analyze + poller.result()?
back: Analysis is an async long-running operation; the SDK polls until done.

front: Content Understanding vs Document Intelligence?
back: CU: multimodal (docs, images, audio, video), semantic schema, generate/classify. DI: structured documents/forms.

front: 3 LLM limitations RAG addresses?
back: Knowledge boundaries (private data), freshness (stale), verifiability (no sources).

front: RAG vs fine-tuning?
back: RAG supplies knowledge at runtime, no weight change, update index not model. Fine-tuning changes model parameters.

front: Keyword vs vector vs hybrid search?
back: Keyword exact terms/codes; vector semantic meaning/paraphrase; hybrid both.

front: Define groundedness.
back: Every claim in the answer is supported by the retrieved context.

front: Foundry IQ components?
back: Knowledge base (domain) → knowledge sources (AI Search index, Blob, SharePoint, OneLake, web) → agentic retrieval (plan, subqueries, rerank, synthesize, cite). Built on Azure AI Search; agents connect via MCP.

front: Role needed by the Foundry project managed identity for Foundry IQ?
back: Search Index Data Reader on the Azure AI Search resource.

front: Azure hierarchy top → bottom?
back: Tenant → subscription (billing) → resource group (folder) → resource.

front: Foundry resource vs project?
back: Resource = Azure resource (models, agent service, quotas, security). Project = workspace inside it for agents, evals, data, indexes.

front: Default deployment type to start with and why? When Data Zone? When Provisioned? When Batch?
back: Global Standard (lowest price, highest quota). Data Zone for US/EU residency. Provisioned (PTU) for predictable throughput/latency. Batch for async 24h jobs ~50% cheaper.

front: Getting 429 rate-limit errors. Two fixes?
back: Reduce max_output_tokens / concurrent requests, or increase TPM quota.

front: Temperature high vs low?
back: High = more creative/varied; low = consistent/deterministic.

front: Two auth methods for endpoints; which for agents via project API?
back: API key or Microsoft Entra ID (DefaultAzureCredential). Project/agent API → Entra ID.

front: Least-privilege role to build agents in a Foundry project? To only call an agent?
back: Foundry User (was Azure AI User); Foundry Agent Consumer.

front: Code to call an agent: client class, credential, method, extra_body?
back: AIProjectClient(endpoint, DefaultAzureCredential()); get_openai_client(); responses.create(input=..., extra_body={'agent':{'name':..., 'type':'agent_reference'}}).

front: Code to chat with a deployed model: class, method, output property?
back: OpenAI(base_url=.../openai/v1/, api_key=...); client.responses.create(model=deployment, input=[...]); response.output_text.
